attribution.note: Marcus wrote this in his own Substack post as a factual assertion. It is not a quote of anyone else.

semantics.note: The short fragment only makes sense with the sentences before it. Together they say the first mention of foundation models/GPAI came in mid-May 2022 from the French government. The normalisation leaves out 'mid-May 2022', but the contract restores it.

contract.note: Marcus said 'first mention', so counting a text that names GPAI in order to exclude it is the ordinary reading, not a stretch. Treating France as acting through its Council presidency is fair. A narrower reading about regulatory obligations is flagged, but it goes beyond his words.

evidence.note: Slovenian presidency's first partial compromise, dated 29 Nov 2021. The excerpt confirms Slovenian provenance and changes to Article 52a; the locator puts the GPAI additions in section II.6. This shows GPAI was treated in a negotiating text before May 2022.
Brussels Privacy Hub analysis from 6 Dec 2021. It reports that the Slovenian-presidency Council text excludes 'general purpose AI systems', independently confirming the 2021 chronology.
French presidency progress report, May 2022. It says France 'revised' existing GPAI provisions, which implies they were already there. It shows French involvement, not a first mention.

reviews.rationale: Marcus says GPAI/foundation models were first mentioned in mid-May 2022, by France. The Slovenian presidency's November 2021 compromise already addressed general-purpose AI, including Article 52a and a scope exclusion. A contemporary December 2021 analysis confirms this. France's May 2022 report describes revising existing GPAI provisions. An earlier text from another presidency therefore exists, which meets the contradiction condition.
